title: I Took the Darkroom Enlarger Timer to the Mentor Who Camped My Easel

parts.text: I stepped into bay two at 7:06 p.m. and mentor Sable was already exposing on my numbered easel. The card said: ONE BAY. NINETY MINUTES. EASEL STAYS WITH THE BOOKING. I was twenty-nine, photo co-op member, holding a tray that listed our chemistry. Sable shrugged. "Mentors are the light." I photographed the card, the booking, and her negative in my carrier. Then I asked for the enlarger log. At 7:14 the tech pinged why Sable's name was on my timer. I kept my voice safelight-soft and let the timestamp talk. A paper card is only paper until someone treats it like a clock.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The tech can see Sable's negative in my carrier during our booking.

social.video_title: She exposed on my numbered easel in my bay — Part 1/2
social.description: Darkroom bay, a mentor on my easel, a ninety-minute timer she posted. I logged the expose. Would you have asked for the enlarger log?

parts.text: Sable called it a test strip until the tech asked for the photo. I printed the ticket, the card, and the carrier still. The easel went back to my handle. Sable ran her own ninety minutes and told the next mentor atmosphere was always about grain. Grain is a word mentors use when a booking exists. Bay policy now has a second line: MENTORS ARE NOT THE LIGHT. I keep our carrier on a labeled hook. Sable brown-bags her jokes. The bay finally looks like a booking, not a loan. The rule looks ordinary now, which is the whole point.

social.video_title: Mentors are not the light — Part 2/2
social.description: Enlarger log, numbered easel, and a second line on the card. Was a test strip ever my carrier?
